journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
title: Multichannel Object Detection for Detecting Suspected Trees With Pine Wilt Disease Using Multispectral Drone Imagery
categories: Journal: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
summary: In this article, a multichannel convolutional neural network (CNN) based object detection was used to detect suspected trees of pine wilt disease after acquiring aerial photographs through a rotorcraft drone equipped with a multispectral camera. The acquired multispectral aerial photographs consist of RGB, green, red, NIR, and red edge spectral bands per shooting point. The aerial photographs for each band performed image calibration to correct radiation distortion, image alignment to correct the distance error of the lenses of a multispectral camera, and image enhancement to edge enhancement to highlight the features of objects in the image. After that, a large amount of data obtained through data augmentation were put into multichannel CNN-based object detection for training and test. As a result of verifying the detection performance of the trained model, excellent detection results were obtained with mAP 86.63% and average intersection over union 71.47%.

AI.tldr: A multichannel CNN object detector fusing five multispectral bands detects pine wilt disease trees from drone imagery, achieving mAP 86.63% and average IoU 71.47%, with no lightweighting or deployment content.
AI.research_relevance: Relevant to remote sensing object detection (drone multispectral imagery) and to multichannel input design, but has no lightweighting or deployment component. Relevance to onboard satellite lightweighting is indirect.

AI.ideas_for_my_research: (1) The multichannel fusion of RGB/NIR/red-edge bands is a transferable idea for small-target detection in vegetation/forest scenes, though not directly applicable to satellite vehicle/ship targets. (2) The preprocessing pipeline (radiometric calibration, alignment, edge enhancement) is a useful reminder that band-level preprocessing quality affects detection, relevant to multispectral satellite data. (3) No lightweighting or deployment content exists, so transfer value to your onboard lightweighting direction is limited to the multichannel-input design pattern.
